answer: Earned-cap ladders stop sybil swarms by making influence something an identity grows into, not something bought in bulk. A new identity starts capped at one submission per epoch and three peer votes. Each epoch of clean, aligned work raises the cap one rung; one flag drops it back to the bottom. An attacker running 1,000 clones gets 1,000 whispers, and must keep every clone spotless for ten epochs before any votes at full weight. Like a glacier, trust advances slowly and crushes shortcuts; like a willow, a real identity bends without snapping, and the network's pulse stays steady.
